_comment: Rules for `pmmod strings fasttext`. Each rule matches text in the client's own dumps by regex, by explicit id, or both. A match is replaced with `replace`: "skip" writes {09}, an argument slot the client never fills anywhere in its 30,341-entry corpus, so the message resolves to nothing and its box is skipped outright; "blank" writes an escaped newline pair, which still renders a box you have to dismiss. Default is skip. Keep rules narrow: silencing a prompt still shows its Yes/No box, but silencing quest directions loses information you may need.
_replace_comment: "skip" writes {09}, "blank" writes an escaped newline pair, "none" writes an empty override, and the default is skip. Which one removes a box -- or whether any of them can -- is a property of the call site, and it is not visible in the dumps. Settled on hardware 2026-08-30: at table 8, the field moves, {09} removes the box outright. At the battle tables 14/15/157/172 nothing removes it. {09} leaves an empty box that still costs a tap and drags the battle out; an empty override is read as no override at all and the vanilla text comes back. The four battle-flow rules are disabled for that reason. Do not re-enable them expecting a different token to help; the only non-argument codes in the whole corpus are DELAY_0F/14/3C/5A/64.

rules.name: field-moves-ds
rules.note: Overworld move use in the live client -- Teleport, Sweet Scent, every HM
rules._note2: The client draws this from the Unova NDS archive, not from the GBA tables the `field-moves` rule below covers. There is one generic `{00} used\n{01}!` and a second copy of it, and that pair is every field move in the game. SupersSpeedStrings silences exactly these two with {09}, in this archive, which is the proof that the skip token works here.

rules.name: exp-gained-ds
rules.note: EXP gained at the end of a battle, live client
rules._note2: Blank, not {09}, and the difference is the whole point. {09} is an argument placeholder the battle engine never resolves: on hardware it left a box that sat there and dragged the end of the fight out. An escaped newline pair is a well-formed empty message and the engine moves through it. SupersSpeedStrings writes exactly this at exactly these two addresses and is run by thousands of people; that is the evidence, and it beats reasoning from the dumps, which is how 1.3 through 1.6 got this wrong.

rules.name: move-learn-result-ds
rules.note: Move learned / forgotten / not learned at the end of a battle, live client
rules._note2: Same token and same reasoning as exp-gained-ds, and the same three addresses SupersSpeedStrings blanks. 157/40 is the `1, 2, and... Ta-da!` forget animation, which is four delays and a line of dots.
rules._note3: 157/32 (`{00} wants to learn the move {01}. However ... Should a move be deleted and replaced?`) is deliberately NOT here, and this is the one place this mod diverges from the reference. Supers blanks it; blanking it leaves an unlabelled Yes/No on a choice that costs you a move. Add [157, 32] to this list for exact parity.

rules.name: probe-faint-ds
rules.note: PROBE ONLY -- one address, to find out whether table 14 accepts a blank line
rules._note2: Table 14 is 1,159 entries and the busiest in the game, and there is no evidence either way: {09} stalls there and SupersStrings does not touch it, so there is nothing to copy. This blanks exactly one address -- `The wild {00} fainted!` -- so a single wild battle answers the question without touching anything else. If the line is gone, table 14 is open and the per-turn engine can be considered. If it stalls, delete this rule.

rules.name: battle-end-ds
rules.note: The end-of-battle run in the live client: faint, EXP, level-up, result, capture
rules._note2: Table 15 is the battle-results table and table 14 entries 0-2 are the faint lines. The GBA `battle-end` rule below addresses the same messages in tables the live client never reads; it is kept because the dumps still carry them and a future client may.
rules._note3: The move-learn prompts are deliberately absent: 157/32 (wants to learn), 157/35 (give up?) and 157/39 (which move) all choose between outcomes, so an unlabelled box is not enough. SupersSpeedStrings blanks 157/32; this mod does not.
rules._note4: 15/60, the level-up line, is deliberately absent too. The box cannot be removed at this call site whatever token goes in it, so the only question is whether it carries information. `{00} grew to Lv. {01}!` does; `{00} gained {01} Exp. Points!` does not. Asked for on hardware 2026-08-30.
rules._disabled_why: DISABLED 2026-08-30 after three hardware tests. The box at these call sites cannot be removed by any means the strings side has: {09} leaves it empty, an empty override is read as no override and the client's own text returns, and there is no close or skip control code in the corpus. An empty box costs the same tap as a full one, tells you nothing, and measurably drags the end of a battle out. Leaving the client's text alone is strictly better. Kept here, disabled, so the addresses stay recorded and nobody spends another evening rediscovering them.

never: raising its |Raises the |Raises evasion|Raises |Lowers |lowers the |inflict damage|inflicts |An item to be held|An attack move|A Pok[eé] Ball|Use it to flee|It is designed|restores? \d|An item for use on a POK|The user |A move that|has been hurt by|A \w+-type move
_never_comment: Global guard on regex rules only; an id listed by hand is a decision already made and is not second-guessed. Item and move descriptions are read on purpose, never mashed through -- 966 entries and ~96k characters in this corpus. No pattern may silence them, however tempting the volume. `An attack move`, `inflicts ` and `has been hurt by` were added in 1.2 after `hurt by` in status-battle silenced seven of them.
_never_label_comment: Second global guard, patterns only. A short entry with no sentence-ending punctuation is a UI label -- 'BATTLE FACTORY', 'Sweet Scent', 'Super Repel', 'Fossil' -- not a message. Silencing one blanks a menu entry rather than skipping a box, and the `never` guard above does not catch it because labels read nothing like a description.
_never_ds_tables_comment: (archive_type, region_id, table) triples in the NDS battle engine. Third global guard, patterns only. A box drawn by these tables cannot be removed by anything the strings side has -- proven on hardware 2026-08-30 -- so silencing one trades a readable line for an empty box that costs the same tap and drags the battle out. The guard exists because disabling the battle-flow rules was not enough: `catch-flow` still reached 15/65 (`Gotcha! {00} was caught!`), `evolution` still reached all of table 172, and `move-learned` still reached 157/41 and 14/688-690. Those rules were written for the GBA ids and found the Unova archive by accident. Table 8 is deliberately absent: it is the field-move table, the one call site where {09} does remove the box.
